question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Secret of the Veda’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Aurobindo.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book **‘The Secret of the Veda' **was written by **Sri Aurobindo.**
 
• This volume comprises Sri Aurobindo’s writings on and translations of the **Rig Veda** that were published in the monthly review '**Arya**' between **1914 **and **1920**.
 
• Most of this material appeared under three headings:
 
 
• **The Secret of the Veda**, August 1914 – July 1916.
 
• **Selected Hymns**, August 1914 – July 1915.
 
• **Hymns of the Atris**, August 1915 – December 1917.
 
 
 
• **Sri Aurobindo **was an Indian nationalist and freedom fighter, a major Indian English poet, philosopher, and yogi.
 
• He joined the movement for India's freedom from British rule and for a duration (1905–10), became one of its most important leaders, before turning to develop his own vision and philosophy of human progress and spiritual evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda**, born **Narendranath Datta**, was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, and author. He was a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna.
 
• **Annie Besant** was a British socialist, theosophist, women's rights activist, writer, orator, political party member, educationist, and philanthropist. Regarded as a champion of human freedom, she was an ardent supporter of both Irish and Indian self-rule. In 1916 she established the Indian Home Rule League, of which she became president. She became the **first woman President of the Indian National Congress **to head the **Calcutta **session of the Indian National Congress in **1917**. 
 
• **Jiddu Krishnamurti **was a philosopher, speaker, and writer. In his early life, he was groomed to be the new World Teacher, an advanced spiritual position in the theosophical tradition, but later rejected this mantle and withdrew from the organization behind it. He was the adopted son of **Annie Besant.**
